It is not a dead end: the GitHub MCP tool GITHUB_COMMIT_MULTIPLE_FILES (owner kavopdf, repo app, branch main, upserts=[{path,content,encoding:utf-8}]) commits several files atomically and worked for all four commits of this run. The next run should commit that way, then 'git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main' so HEAD matches origin, then chain.py. chain.py's sync check is strict SHA equality and also refuses a dirty tree, and it rewrites CHAIN.json - so commit CHAIN.json again after each chain.py run.

context: THE SPILL WAS THE CARRY'S CEILING, NOT A ROW HEIGHT. The carry-over asked for a fourth wrap-charge build (page-layout this time); this run measured that on 041122 the row does not need to be taller - it needs the renderer to wrap it the way the page did, and the mechanism for that (ARIAL_W, w:w) was already in the engine and silently not clamping on merged cells. carryScalePct was given colTw[c], the FIRST grid column under the cell, so on a cell merged over six columns the width was negative, the clamp was skipped, and the scale went out at the page's drawn ratio 97 % where the cell allows 92. Four of the page's nine instruction lines wrapped into two, the row rendered 154 pt where the page drew 118, and it no longer fitted the 158 pt the page had left. Fix is one token (spanTw - pInset). Corpus diff: 3 of 213 .docx change, 210 byte-identical, all 3 measured: 373_leave_application_form 5.46 -> 4.64, 041122 11 -> 10 pages, Account_Opening_Form_Fillable_filled 11 -> 10 pages, 0 worse. THE CLASS DOES NOT MOVE YET because the last spurious page of both form documents is a FOLIO WRITTEN AS A TABLE ROW (the declaration table's last row is the bare text '7'), which costs its own sheet and shifts every page after it - our page 8 reads share@5 99.02 with text_recall 0.04. The flow-line folio rule exists and names this document but cannot fire on a table row. THE ONE THING THE NEXT RUN SHOULD DO: make that row a position - detect it before the row loop, skip it, take the last-row bookkeeping from row-1, emit the text after </w:tbl> via anchor(sb, ctx, x, yTop, w, h, inner), which needs only a hand-built paragraph string. w:framePr does NOT work as the cheap route (anchored to the page at y 16104 tw it rendered at y 218 pt). That one change should take both form documents from 10 pages to the source's 9 and is what moves the class.
